OPEN
This is open, and cannot be resolved with a finite computation.
Let $k\geq 3$ and define $g_k(n)$ to be the minimal $N$ such that $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ contains some $A$ of size $\lvert A\rvert=n$ such that\[\langle A\rangle = \left\{\sum_{a\in A}\epsilon_aa: \epsilon_a\in \{0,1\}\right\}\]contains no non-trivial $k$-term arithmetic progression. Estimate $g_k(n)$. In particular, is it true that\[g_3(n) \gg 3^n?\]
#817: [Er91]
additive combinatorics
A problem of Erdős and Sárközy who proved\[g_3(n) \gg \frac{3^n}{n^{O(1)}}.\]

 Two small additions to the recent progress on the case $k=3$ (Korsky, arXiv:2606.24139; Costa, arXiv:2609.06303). Throughout, call a set $A$ of $n$ distinct positive integers admissible if $\langle A\rangle$ contains no non-trivial 3-term AP; by Korsky's Proposition 4.1 this is equivalent to the $3^n$ sums $\sum_i c_ia_i$, $c\in\{0,1,2\}^n$, being pairwise distinct. Equivalently, since $\{0,1,2\}^n-\{0,1,2\}^n=\{-2,\dots,2\}^n$ coordinatewise, no non-zero $c\in\{-2,\dots,2\}^n$ satisfies $\sum_i c_ia_i=0$; I use this second form below.
1. From $\liminf$ to $\lim$. If $A\subseteq[N]$ is admissible with $|A|=n$, then $\{1\}\cup 3A\subseteq[3N]$ is admissible with $n+1$ elements: a relation $c_0+\sum_i c_i\,(3a_i)=0$ with $c\in\{-2,\dots,2\}^{n+1}$ forces $3\mid c_0$, hence $c_0=0$, and then $c=0$ by the admissibility of $A$. Therefore
$$g_3(n+1)\;\le\;3\,g_3(n)\qquad(n\ge1),$$
so the sequence $g_3(n)/3^n$ is non-increasing. Consequently Costa's Corollary 1.2, $\liminf_{n\to\infty} g_3(n)/3^n=0$, already gives
$$\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{g_3(n)}{3^n}=0,\qquad\text{i.e. } g_3(n)=o(3^n)\ \text{along all } n,$$
not only along the subsequences $n=d\ell$ of his Theorem 1.1. (This assumes Costa's result. On the proof-claim thread, 7 Sep 2026, he reports a self-contained Lean 4 verification starting from the Formal Conjectures statement Erdos817.erdos_817, which formalises only the "in particular" question, and concluding answer(False); the code is in the updated record doi:10.5281/zenodo.22638810. I have not checked that verification myself.) Monotonicity also turns every exact value into a bound for all larger $n$: $g_3(n)\le g_3(n_0)\,3^{\,n-n_0}$ for $n\ge n_0$.
2. Exact values for $n=5,6$. Extending the table in Korsky's Remark 4.6 (which covers $n\le4$), an exhaustive search over $n$-subsets of $[N]$, testing the ternary distinctness with a bitmask dynamic programme and cross-checked by an independent implementation (and, for $n\le4$, directly from the definition), gives
$$g_3(5)=60,\qquad g_3(6)=168,$$
with witnesses $\{38,52,57,59,60\}$ and $\{107,145,159,162,166,168\}$; every $N\le167$ is excluded for $n=6$. Compared with Korsky's lower bound $b_n=(T_n-1)/2+\sum_{j<n}T_j$ ($T_j=[x^j](1+x+x^2)^j$ the central trinomial coefficient), which equals $21,56,152$ for $n=4,5,6$ (and $b_7=419$), the gap $g_3(n)-b_n$ is $1,4,16$. By item 1,
$$g_3(n)\;\le\;\frac{168}{729}\,3^n\;<\;0.2305\cdot3^n\qquad\text{for all } n\ge6,$$
an explicit improvement of the trivial $g_3(n)\le 3^{n-1}$ (the ratios $g_3(n)/3^n$ for $n=1,\dots,6$ are $0.333,0.333,0.296,0.272,0.247,0.230$). Two remarks on the extremal sets:
(a) The powers of $3$ are not optimal for $n\ge3$, although $\{1,3,\dots,3^{n-1}\}$ is the unique admissible set minimising $\sum_i a_i^2$ (for admissible $A$ the $3^n$ ternary sums are distinct integers, so the variance $\tfrac23\sum_i a_i^2$ of a uniform ternary sum is at least $(9^n-1)/12$, with equality iff the sums are consecutive, i.e. iff $A$ consists of the powers of $3$).
(b) For each $n\le5$ there is an optimal set of the form $\{G_n-G_k:0\le k<n\}$ with $(G_n)=0,1,3,8,22,60$, the same "offsets from the maximum reproduce the sequence" phenomenon as in the Conway–Guy sets for distinct subset sums. The pattern breaks at $n=6$: the value $164=2(60+22)$ suggested by the recursion $G_n=2(G_{n-1}+G_{n-2})$ is excluded, and the optimum $168$ has offsets $\{0,2,6,9,23,61\}$.
The initial terms $1,3,8,22,60,168$ coincide with those of OEIS A318821 and A318863, which count rooted trees with a prescribed maximal multiplicity of subtrees; I see no reason to expect a connection. Both continue with $466$, and by the above $419\le g_3(7)\le 504$, so the value $g_3(7)$ would decide whether the coincidence persists (the search for $n=7$ is beyond the simple enumeration used here). I intend to submit $g_3(n)$ to the OEIS as a separate sequence unless someone recognises it.
So, for $k=3$, the current state is
$$\Bigl(\tfrac{\sqrt3}{2\sqrt\pi}+o(1)\Bigr)\frac{3^n}{\sqrt n}\;\le\;g_3(n)\;=\;o(3^n),$$
with the exact values known for $n\le6$. (On the proof-claim thread Xiao Hu notes that this is not a full solution since Erdős and Sárközy asked for an estimate, while Costa replies that he regards the question $g_3(n)\gg3^n$ itself as the main one; either way, the true rate between $3^n/\sqrt n$ and $o(3^n)$ is open.)

 I have a short preprint on arXiv: https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.24139 proving some lower and upper bounds for this problem.
For $k=3$, I prove the finite bound
$$
g_3(n)\ge \frac{T_n-1}{2}+\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}T_j,\qquad T_m=[x^m](1+x+x^2)^m.
$$
Thus
$$
g_3(n)\ge \left(\frac{\sqrt3}{2\sqrt\pi}+o(1)\right)\frac{3^n}{\sqrt n},
$$
improving the earlier $3^n/n$ lower bound of Erdős and Sárközy. The proof uses the equivalence between 3AP-freeness of $H(A)$ and injectivity of all ternary sums $\sum_i\varepsilon_i a_i$, $\varepsilon_i\in{0,1,2}$, together with the exact bandwidth of the ternary grid. 
Note that it is also easy to get a lower bound of the order $\Omega(3^n/\sqrt{n})$ (with worse constant than the more involved argument above) with the classic second moment argument that analogously attains a $\Omega(2^n/\sqrt{n})$ bound for the distinct subset sum problem. This would already beat the Erdős and Sárközy $\Omega(3^n/n)$ bound.
For fixed $k\ge4$, I prove
$$
g_k(n)\gg_k \left(\frac{k-1}{k-2}\right)^n n^{-\log_2((k-1)/(k-2))}.
$$
The local chain step in the proof also gives an improvement for Hilbert cubes in $k$-AP-free sets, replacing the Dietmann--Elsholtz growth base $k/(k-1)$ by $(k-1)/(k-2)$. The polynomial factor above comes from an additional averaging argument using the distinctness of the subset-sum generators.
There is also a complementary construction using the standard idea of digit-restricted sets in base $p$ (for $p$ prime) showing
$$
\limsup_{n\to\infty}g_k(n)^{1/n}\le \min_{p\ge3\ \mathrm{prime}}p^{2/(\min{p,k}-1)}.
$$

 Thanks, although I note that Erdős did not report what exponent they achieved in the $O(1)$ notation (in particular he never claimed a lower bound of $3^n/n$ as you say). It is entirely possible (although since this is unpublished we can not know for sure) that they were already aware of the bound $\gg 3^n/\sqrt{n}$ (indeed this seems likely, since Erdős was of course very familiar with the method that achieved $2^n/\sqrt{n}$ for [1], which basically works here also as you say). I believe that the real problem Erdős had in mind is whether $g_3(n)\gg 3^n$ (and so he probably didn't spend too much time thinking about how to optimise the constant).

A full proof 
claimed by Simone Costa (using ChatGPT (OpenAI, GPT-5.6 Sol)).
 Summary:
 I have just posted a preprint giving a negative answer to the question in Problem 817. More precisely, I prove
$$\liminf_{n\to\infty}\frac{g_3(n)}{3^n}=0.$$
The argument combines Korsky's characterization in terms of ternary coefficient sums with a consequence of the OpenAI construction for Erdős Problem 1, followed by a base-three expansion.
Preprint: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22313501
ChatGPT (OpenAI, GPT-5.6 Sol) was used in developing and checking the argument and in revising the manuscript; the full AI declaration is included in the paper. I have checked the mathematical statements and references and take responsibility for the proof.
